title: Inference operational alignment & cost sprint kickoff
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-11 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Leah Carter (Redwood AE), Jonas Park (Redwood SE), Holly Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Maya Singh (Mariner), Oliver Grant (Mariner), Priya Rao (Mariner), Evan Ortiz (Mariner)
summary: Quarterly health + cost sprint kickoff to align on usage trends, cost pressure points, reliability issues during peak hours, and agree pilot scope for Dedicated capacity trial. Agreed next steps: send model-level cost breakdown, security appendix, and schedule 2-day on-prem stress test in Jan.
topics: usage trend and token burn analysis
action_items: Leah Carter: Provide model-by-model cost & p95 latency CSV and short memo by 2026-12-15
Jonas Park: Spin up lightweight benchmark (5k requests) config for Mariner's 512-token flows and share results by 2026-12-20
Priya Rao: Share network diagram and egress constraints; due 2026-12-18
Holly Nguyen: Draft pilot acceptance criteria and dashboard access list by 2026-12-16
next_steps: Redwood to send security appendix (SOC2 report + KMS integration notes)
Schedule 2-day on-prem / VPC stress test (Jan 11-12) pending network details
Customer to review Dedicated capacity proposal and respond with headcount/finance constraints w/in 7 days
transcript:
[00:00] Leah Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick sanity check, can you all hear me?
[00:03] Maya Singh: Yep, loud and clear. thanks.
[00:06] Leah Carter: Awesome. goal for today is a short QBR-style health sync but also kick off the cost-reduction sprint we chatted about. we'll surface usage patterns, latency pain points, and propose a pilot for Dedicated capacity. Jonas, wanna take the data slide?
[00:18] Jonas Park: Sure. I've got the usage trends pulled — tokens per day jumped 42% month over month since August, and the 95th percentile token length increased from ~320 to ~460 — which amplifies latency and KV cache pressure. you're seeing more long-form summarization flows.
[00:32] Priya Rao: that's right, the new "patient-note-assembly" pipeline spools a lot of context. We're seeing spikes aligned with our evening digest job between 18:00 and 21:00 UTC.
[00:40] Oliver Grant: to be clear, our immediate ask is to shave down cost without increasing tail latency beyond 200ms for our synchronous endpoints.
[00:48] Jonas Park: Understood. A few levers we usually recommend: prefix/KV caching for repeated context, reduce generation temperature where acceptable, and pilot a quantized model variant on Dedicated to drop GPU utilization. Redwood Optimize can produce suggestions for batching thresholds too.
[01:05] Evan Ortiz: quick question — when you say Dedicated, do you mean reserved GPU pools that you host, or something on-prem? we have compliance constraints for some PHI datasets.
[01:12] Leah Carter: Good callout. Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved pools in a customer-dedicated tenancy (data isolated). For PHI we typically advise Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem installation) — we can run an on-prem package for air-gapped workloads. both options integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.
[01:26] Maya Singh: We're aiming for SOC2 level controls. do you have the SOC2 report and details about audit logs and retention?
[01:31] Holly Nguyen: Yes — we'll attach the security appendix after the call. it includes SOC2 report, how audit logs are surfaced in the Console, SAML SSO setup steps, RBAC primitives, and KMS integration notes.
[01:40] Priya Rao: On the network side, we have strict egress windows and an existing proxy that terminates TLS. this may affect direct-hosted API calls, so we need VPC peering or an on-prem option.
[01:50] Jonas Park: That's fine; for VPC we support private endpoints and can do customer-managed NAT for egress. for the stress test, we'll need the network diagram and a small set of test credentials.
[02:05] Oliver Grant: cost modeling — can you show our current spend per 1000 inference calls roughly? last month finance flagged a 3x increase.
[02:13] Jonas Park: Rough high-level: your current hosted mix is ~70% gpt-like open models at the default quantization, and unit cost per 1k tokens is around $0.34 in December pricing. With dedicated, using a quantized variant and autoscale pooling, we estimate a 25-40% reduction in per-token cost for your 512-token median flows, depending on utilization and batching.
[02:35] Maya Singh: those are estimates. what's the risk to output quality when moving to the quantized variant? dark question.
[02:40] Jonas Park: It'll vary by prompt set. Redwood Optimize has a model/regression harness; we typically run a 500-prompt eval to detect regressions. in our experience, 4-bit quantization on these architectures has modest quality drift but often acceptable for extraction and summarization tasks. we'll validate on your test set.
[02:58] Evan Ortiz: Any timeline for the pilot?
[03:00] Leah Carter: propose a pilot timeline: dec 15 — we deliver model-level cost & latency CSV + Dedicated commercial bands; dec 20 — run a lightweight benchmark for your 512-token flows; jan 11-12 — 2-day on-prem/VPC stress test pending network details; then a 4-week pilot window on Dedicated in mid-Jan. sound reasonable?
[03:19] Oliver Grant: yes, but finance needs firm numbers. can you give two commercial bands — conservative and aggressive — and what headroom they'd require?
[03:27] Leah Carter: we'll provide three pricing bands: conservative (low utilization reserved), balanced (typical commit), and aggressive (higher commit, lower unit price) with break-even points.
[03:36] Maya Singh: aside from Dedicated, are there quick wins we can do in the next two weeks?
[03:40] Jonas Park: Absolutely. low-effort wins: enable prefix caching for the patient-note pipeline, set aggregation window to align with your digest job to increase batching, and use a slightly lower token budget for non-sensitive summarization. these have landed customers 8–20% cost drop before any infra changes.
[03:55] Priya Rao: caching sounds simple but we need to ensure consistency. the KV cache invalidation rules need to be aligned with our data freshness SLA.
[04:03] Holly Nguyen: We'll propose cache TTL recommendations tailored to Mariner's freshness requirements and include a short runbook for invalidation.
[04:10] Maya Singh: Security follow-ups: SSO for the Console is required, and we need role separation for dev vs prod. also can we get an audit log retention option of 2 years?
[04:18] Holly Nguyen: SSO/SAML is standard, RBAC supports arbitrary groups and roles; audit log retention can be configured — we'll include the options and any storage cost implications in the appendix.
[04:28] Evan Ortiz: Are there known issues with p95 latency spikes when you have long token sequences and low batching? we've seen 800ms spikes.
[04:35] Jonas Park: Long sequences and low batching do increase p95. some mitigation: reduce sequence length where possible, dynamic batching thresholds that favor shorter requests, and fallback to a smaller model variant during high load windows. smart routing can route traffic to cheaper variants when tail latency is acceptable.
[04:53] Oliver Grant: fallback worries me — we don't want user-facing hallucinations to increase.
[04:58] Jonas Park: Totally fair. we recommend traffic shadowing for the fallback paths and monitor a prompt-level quality metric before flipping any routing rules. Redwood Console has rollout controls and automatic rollback on regression signals.
[05:12] Maya Singh: can you remind me what rollout controls are available?
[05:15] Leah Carter: Canary deploys, percentage-based traffic splits, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback policies by error/latency/quality thresholds. all visible in the Console's per-route dashboards.
[05:25] Priya Rao: For the stress test, we need to validate KV cache warmup behavior. historically our workloads have cold-cache penalties early in the window.
[05:33] Jonas Park: We'll instrument cache-warm sequences in the benchmark and provide heatmaps for warm vs cold requests.
[05:40] Holly Nguyen: ok, quick recap of decisions and owners: Redwood to send cost/latency CSV (Leah), run lightweight bench (Jonas), security appendix (Holly). Mariner to share network diagram and egress constraints (Priya) and confirm pilot acceptance criteria (Evan + Maya).
[05:58] Oliver Grant: can we get a single doc summarizing the pilot scope, acceptance criteria, and rollback plan?
[06:03] Leah Carter: Yes — Holly will draft the pilot spec doc and circulate by Dec 16.
[06:08] Evan Ortiz: one more ask — can you include an example dashboard view for per-route token burn and p95 latency so our finance team understands the drivers?
[06:16] Holly Nguyen: We'll attach a Console screenshot and an exportable CSV template.
[06:21] Maya Singh: Great. any blockers from Redwood side we should be aware of?
[06:24] Jonas Park: only dependency is network details for the on-prem/VPC test and service account access.
[06:30] Leah Carter: ok let's close quick. next steps — Leah will email the three pricing bands and the model cost CSV by Dec 15, Jonas will run the bench and post results by Dec 20, Holly sends pilot doc by Dec 16, Mariner provides network diagram by Dec 18.
[06:44] Oliver Grant: sounds good, thanks.
[06:46] Leah Carter: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email. bye.
[06:50] (call ends)
notes: Customer is sensitive to PHI compliance; on-prem/VPC options required for portions of workload
Primary levers: Dedicated + quantized variant, caching, batching, routing policies
Finance requires hard break-even points for different commit levels
